It took a while to get here, but I've finally found the perfect alternative to standard K-cup pods.  I didn't like using the usual K-cup coffee because they held about half the coffee I'd prefer and that most of them weren't recyclable.  I also wanted to use my own favorite coffee.  So, I opted for the reusable plastic K-cup pods and they were fine, and with no problem holding a full two tablespoons of coffee grounds.  The problem though, was that the remaining grounds went into the sink and it didn't take long for them to stain the porcelain.  So, I decided to try the paper filters for the reusable pods, knowing that the filters could be put in the trash after use.  The problem though, was that because they are not intended to fit all the way down to the floor of the reusable pods, it couldn't give me the two tablespoons of ground coffee that I wanted.  So, back they went.  Then I found the iFill Single Fill Pods.  I was a bit skeptical at first and was frankly surprised that I was able to put all two tablespoons of coffee into them and that the fastened lid snapped tightly shut.  I didn't have to wiggle the pod around in the unit to get it to fit, and it brewed the perfect cup of coffee for me.  As a bonus, for some reason they are quieter than the other pods as they are brewing and I can toss the used pods as soon as the drip completes.  The one thing I hope for is that there eventually be competition for this product so that the price can come down a bit.  For what they a

The first couple I didn’t have any problems. The other 15 or so like others have mentioned all 5 of the holes on the keurig supreme does not puncture. So my solution is now to put the pod in close the top to puncture. Open the top to check to make sure all 5 holes have punched thru. The ones that have not punctured I just use a toothpick to make sure all 5 holes are open and reclose the unit before brewing coffee. The holes that have not puncture is very easy with a toothpick.  Is this aggravating yes. But not having coffee grounds all over the place from using the extra pod supplied by keurig  makes this a win for me. I can just throw it in a brew without having to prepare and pull out the big can of coffee every morning. I filled all of these pods at one time using the entire can of coffee. Convenience for the win. If they figure out how to make the top tighter so it puncture ms all holes at one time this will definitely be a five star product. Will I buy again as they are? Yes. Just have my toothpick handy. Coffee on people! :)

When I found I wasn't needing to make full pots of coffee anymore... it was just ending up getting cold... I bought a single brew machine.  But I still really enjoy my own coffee rather than the pre-filled pods.  Those are either too blah or too strong/sharp.  So I started with the reusable pods... that gave me coffee grounds and bitter taste.  Then added little filters.  Better, but still not getting that good coffee flavor I was getting before in my regular full pot machine.  Then recently I found these iFillCup pods on Amazon.  Had to give it try.  So, confession, I don't always read directions first... (I'm sure I'm not alone in that).  The first try was less than great.  I overfilled it and packed it down to get as much coffee in there as I could.  My machine did not like that.  Steam and flashing lights, but no damage, thank goodness.  So next I saw the package very clearly labeled, saying where the fill line is and not to pack it down.  Geez... silly me.  Now I fill it with my own ground coffee, more finely ground than for regular brew, to the proper fill level.  And I do pack it down very lightly, rather than cram in as much coffee as possible.  I'm happy.  And I'm good with recycling these pods.  I can see that it is possible to reuse them, but I think coffee flavor may be sacrificed.  I definitely recommend this product.

Like many other reviewers, I have tried a myriad of fillable coffee pods.  I've cannibalized various products to create what my wife called "Frankencups".  I've tried combinations of used K-cups, filters, filters with flaps, mix and matched lids with cups, and pre-punctured many lids.  Finally I created something that worked but the result was a weaker than expected cup of coffee and holding the machines "head" unit down tight was necessary.  Even after all that, I had to clean up many of the reusable pieces. Then, these ifill cups showed up on Prime Day deals- probably suggested because  of all the previous products I've purchased and tried.  For me, it is a game changer. As soon as they arrived, I was impressed by the packaging and the quality of the ifill cups.  I immediately filled one with an espresso grind, 2x caffeine coffee.  The lid sealed like it was some tight tolerance machined part. A nice solid feel.  I threw it in my K-cup Express machine and started to hold the lid of the machine down tight to keep excess water from mixing with coffee.  I had to stop myself and see if these cups would produce a single stream of coffee.  EUREKA !  It worked flawlessly.  I savored my very first decent cup of coffee made with ANY fillable cup.  I checked the ifillsystems website and saw they have a brewer.  My thinking is if their brewer is anything like the pods, I must get one.
